findings.requirement: Receipt provenance must enforce the declared post-freeze creation invariant and reject receipts whose immutable origin is a descendant of the population-freeze commit.
findings.evidence: scripts/mros/population_git_trust.py:88-101 accepts any receipt origin other than the freeze commit when git merge-base --is-ancestor freeze origin succeeds. A receipt created in a descendant commit therefore produces no error, although it was created after population freeze. The same implementation's regression test only covers a post-freeze receipt as valid, so the bypass remains directly executable.
findings.falsifier: A trusted-queue regression test that creates the population manifest at commit F, creates a valid receipt at descendant commit R, points QUEUE_REF at R, and proves load_exact_receipts returns a provenance error would falsify this finding.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Replace descendant ancestry acceptance with an explicit provenance rule matching the frozen contract: distinguish the allowed receipt creation event from later replacement or unauthorized descendant history, enforce exactly one immutable origin at the expected post-freeze execution boundary, and add a regression test for descendant replacement/late receipt scenarios.
